start.notes: The company issue: a wired terminal with modem and slip printer, the mail and labels discs, a few empty boxes, three small cells, a knife, a little ore and scrap, and what you carried from the old life. No charger, no smelter, no recycler: the first ten minutes decide what to buy with 50 credits.

machines.name: Your hands
machines.desc: Two hands and a bench of habit. Cutting, stacking, filling, packing: instant, no cells, no energy.
machines.notes: Virtual: not a thing, always owned. Hand recipes are instant, 0 energy, 0 cells.

machines.name: Workbench
machines.desc: A steel bench with a vice, a roller and a rack of hand tools. Repair, refill, bundle, refurbish.

machines.name: Smelter
machines.desc: The old cast-iron furnace, its firebox gutted for a cell rack. Two ore in, one bar out.
machines.notes: Keeps the furnace footprint 3x4 and its ore-in crucible. Composition is iron and firebrick (silicate). Buildable: see rcp_mach_build_smelter.

machines.name: Recycler
machines.desc: A grinding drum and a row of sorting chutes. Anything in, materials out, a tenth to sludge.

machines.name: Crusher
machines.desc: Twin toothed rollers over a steel hopper. Breaks mixed scrap, e-waste and ice into sorted lumps.

machines.name: Purifier
machines.desc: A tall tank with a pump and a filter sleeve. Greywater or melted ice goes in, clean water comes out.

machines.name: Charger
machines.desc: A wall-fed cradle that trickles station power into a spent cell. Billed by the charge, at the power price.

effects.text: Refills a cell for its capacity x the power price, in credits
Charges overnight too; a brownout slows it

machines.notes: Generic rule: any cell in the cradle is refilled; no matter moves. The effects text is the visible price. Buildable: see rcp_mach_build_charger.

machines.name: Hydro tray
machines.desc: A shallow polymer tray with a drip line and a lamp bracket. Seed, water and light turn over nights to crops.

machines.name: Wired terminal
machines.desc: An all-in-one machine with a curved green screen and a floppy drive. It runs on a cell and a wall socket.
machines.notes: Numbers carried from src/kinds.json (memory 640, disk 2048, speed 8).

machines.name: Modem
machines.desc: A beige box with a handset cradle and a line jack. Plugs into the terminal: no modem, no mail.

effects.text: Mail orders reach you: +1 per day (none without a modem)
Lets wholesale and attachment mail through

machines.notes: orders_per_day add is the modem share of the phase rate; task 10 owns the base rate.

machines.name: Slip printer
machines.desc: A thermal slot printer with a roll of paper tape. Order slips, labels and receipts, a strip at a time.

machines.name: Box sealer
machines.desc: A clamp frame with a tape head and a hot wire. Run a packed box through and it comes out sealed.

machines.name: Scanner
machines.desc: A flat bed under a hooded lamp, wired to a sensor head. Shows what a box or a disc is hiding.

effects.text: Security inspection chance -5% while a scanner is powered

machines.name: Radio
machines.desc: A scuffed engineers' set tuned to the maintenance bands. Chatter about breakdowns before they happen.

recipes.name: Crush mixed scrap
recipes.notes: iron 1 + polymer 1 + copper 0.5 in, same out: copper arrives half the time.

recipes.name: Crush e-waste
recipes.notes: Expected: rare dust 0.3 and noble flake 0.1 per board. A board is worth 9; the dust and flake alone are worth 6.1.

recipes.name: Crush ice
recipes.notes: Melts and splits: water and gas. No sludge, unlike the recycler.

recipes.name: Melt iron scrap
recipes.notes: Scrap becomes a bar with no slag: two units in, two out.

recipes.name: Patch a spare part
recipes.notes: Four iron scrap and a flake of polymer, hammered and glued. Five patched spares.

recipes.name: Rework patched spares
recipes.notes: Spare part, route 1 of 3: ten patched spares stripped, shimmed and re-bushed to standard.

recipes.name: Grow greens
recipes.notes: Greywater is fine for leaves. Seed 0.2 + water 1 + nutrient 1.2 = 2.4 in; crop 2.3 + 0.7 x 0.2 seed out.

recipes.name: Purify ice
recipes.notes: Ice is water 2 + volatiles 1: the gas must come out as a bladder, not loss.

recipes.name: Melt ice
recipes.notes: No filter worn: rough meltwater, cheap and spine-grade.

recipes.name: Empty oxygen canister
recipes.notes: Using a canister returns the empty shell.

recipes.name: Mix sugar wash
recipes.notes: Yeast would speed it; the pinned food chain keeps it optional.

recipes.name: Rinse water filter
recipes.notes: Filters are renewable for a pouch of water and an energy; the grime comes out as sludge. Tune uses on the filter if it proves too cheap.

recipes.name: Seal small box
recipes.notes: A box ships only sealed and with an order slip inside; the sealer does not check the slip.

recipes.name: Cut a box open
recipes.notes: The knife wears one use per cut.

recipes.name: Hide goods under padding

effects.text: Inspection chance +3% if the box is found

recipes.notes: A false bottom: a hidden box passes a casual look but not the scanner.

recipes.name: Clear a jam with a kit

effects.text: Frees a jammed feed, no wrench needed

recipes.name: Flash the controller
recipes.notes: Costly and blunt; prog_antivirus does it cheaper and finds the disc that carried it.

recipes.name: Repair goods
recipes.notes: Worth less than new, more than broken.

effects.text: Shows false bottoms and hidden contents
Shows mod_infected, mod_bad_sector and mod_cracked on a disc
Marks contraband and fakes (mod_counterfeit, mod_stolen); inspection chance -5% for a day

recipes.name: Print order slips
recipes.notes: Paper 0.5 fibre becomes five slips of 0.1. prog_labels runs on the terminal that feeds the printer. Slips are pinned at 0.2 each: five come out for a sheet worth 2, so the value warning is expected (the slip is a ticket, not goods).

items.name: Iron scrap
items.desc: A fist of bent iron offcuts, rust-red where the paint has gone. One unit of iron.
items.notes: Fab smelts and rolls it; recycler output.

items.name: Copper scrap
items.desc: Stripped copper, still curled from the conduit it came out of. One unit of copper.
items.notes: Wire and tool stock; recycler output.

items.name: Light scrap
items.desc: Pale alloy bent off a ladder rail or a duct frame. Light enough for one hand.
items.notes: Fab (extruder, smelter) feedstock.

items.name: Grit
items.desc: Coarse pale sand ground from stone and old glass. Scours, fills, and melts into glass.
items.notes: Fab (kiln, glass) feedstock.

items.name: Carbon dust
items.desc: Black dust that coats the hand and stays. Out of old filters, burnt husks and duct soot.
items.notes: Machines (filters) and fab (steel) feedstock.

items.name: Polymer flake
items.desc: Grey chips of crushed plastic, bagged. Warm to the touch when fresh. Becomes sheet and casing.
items.notes: Fab (extruder) feedstock.

items.name: Fibre lint
items.desc: A grey wad of lint and short fibre pulled from filters and bedding. Soft, dusty, useful.
items.notes: Lux (pulper, loom) feedstock.

items.name: Biomass paste
items.desc: A grey brick of pressed paste, cold and faintly sweet. What the vats are fed.
items.notes: Food (vat) feedstock. Also made by the digester.

items.name: Greywater
items.desc: A sealed flask of cloudy water. Not for drinking until it has been through a purifier.
items.notes: Life (purifier) feedstock; meltwater siphoned off the ice haul (sys_ice_haul).

items.name: Salt cake
items.desc: A pale crust of mineral salt, scraped off the reclaim tanks and pressed into a cake.
items.notes: Life (scrubbers, brine) feedstock.

items.name: Reagent dregs
items.desc: Dark, mixed chemical dregs in a stoppered vial. A chemist can work with it. Nobody else should.
items.notes: Med (chem bench) feedstock.

items.name: Gas bladder
items.desc: A tight, flat bladder of mixed gas, strapped to a carry-frame. Handle with care; do not puncture.
items.notes: Life (electrolyser, scrubber) feedstock.

items.name: Sludge
items.desc: A sealed jug of brown slurry that is all that remains of other things. Digest it or vent it.
items.notes: Digester and vent input; the recycler's 10% ends up here.

items.name: Iron ore
items.desc: Red-brown rock off the ore haul, banded with rust. Two lumps make a bar.
items.notes: Hauled in by sys_ore_haul. Smelter feed.

items.name: Copper ore
items.desc: Green-crusted rock off the haul. Smells of pennies when it is crushed.
items.notes: Hauled in by sys_ore_haul.

items.name: Bauxite
items.desc: Pitted red-brown bauxite, light for its size. The only source of fresh light metal.
items.notes: Hauled in by sys_ore_haul.

items.name: Ice block
items.desc: A dirty block of comet ice, grey with dust and hard to hold. Water and gas, once it melts.
items.notes: Hauled in by sys_ice_haul.

items.name: Mixed scrap
items.desc: A lot of junk bagged together: bent iron, plastic housings, a few lengths of wire. Crush or recycle it.
items.notes: Spine salvage lot; the crusher sorts it better than the recycler.

items.name: E-waste
items.desc: A stack of dead boards and cracked screens. Worth more crushed than whole.
items.notes: Source of rare dust and noble flakes (crusher).

items.name: Rags
items.desc: A tied bundle of stained cloth off the spine bunks. Fibre for the pulper, and not much else.
items.notes: Pulper and loom feed.

items.name: Slag
items.desc: Glassy grey clinker raked out of the smelter. The kiln can use it.
items.notes: Mainly a smelting byproduct (fab recipes); old heaps are also swept up as salvage.

items.name: Duct junk
items.desc: A tangle of foil tape, fan housings and ducting yanked from the spine walls.
items.notes: Pulled by spine scavengers. Crusher yields light scrap, polymer flake and lint.

items.name: Hull offcuts
items.desc: Heavy plates and strips of hull alloy, cut off during repair and left on the dock.
items.notes: Left behind by dock repair crews (sys_ore_haul upkeep). Crusher splits iron from light metal.

items.name: Wire tangle
items.desc: A knotted ball of cable, half stripped, with a few cracked connectors still hanging off.
items.notes: Spine rewiring leaves these. Crusher splits copper from insulation.

items.name: Rubble
items.desc: A heavy bag of broken panel, concrete grit and old filter fill, swept from the dock floor.
items.notes: Dock sweepings. Crush for grit, iron flecks and carbon; or vent it.

items.name: Spent filters
items.desc: Clogged cartridge husks from the scrubber bank, black inside and smelling of old breath.
items.notes: Swapped out by sys_scrubber_bank crews. Crusher gives carbon dust, lint and salt.

items.name: Salvage crate
items.desc: A battered lidded crate from a clearance sale, packed with whatever a scavenger could not sell.
items.notes: Composition is the empty shell. A first lot of the spine scavengers; opening it is the point.

items.name: Noble flake
items.desc: A pinch of gold-bright flakes in a sealed twist of foil. It never tarnishes.
items.notes: Fab (contacts, jewellery) feedstock. Wave B: some trader should sell it.

items.name: Rare dust
items.desc: Grey, greasy dust that clings to the fingers. The magnets and chips are made of this.
items.notes: Tech (chips, magnets) feedstock. Wave B: some trader should sell it.

items.name: Lithium salt
items.desc: White, caking salt in a screw-top tub. It holds a charge the way nothing else does.
items.notes: Tech (cells) feedstock.

items.name: Dead cell husk
items.desc: A drained cell casing, split down the seam. A little lithium still clings to the inside.
items.notes: Dock chargers throw these out. Crusher recovers the lithium as salt.

items.name: Iron bar
items.desc: Grey bar cast in a mould, a hollow on top where it cooled. Smelted from ore or scrap.

items.name: Steel sheet
items.desc: Rolled thin from a bar, edges still sharp. Two to a bar.

items.name: Copper wire
items.desc: A coil of bare copper, a few metres. Four to a bar.

items.name: Fasteners
items.desc: A tin of bolts and rivets, sorted by feel. Never enough of them.

items.name: Tin can
items.desc: Empty can and lid, rolled and crimped. Food goes in, and stays in.
items.notes: Vessel for food: food recipes can can rations in these. Sink is the food worker.

items.name: Kitchen knife
items.desc: Kitchen steel in a polymer grip. Cuts cheese, salami, bread and sealed boxes. Wears.

items.name: Wrench
items.desc: Forged jaw on a long arm, worn bright where the hand goes. Clears jams, fits parts. Wears.

items.name: Hinge
items.desc: Two leaves and a pin. Doors, lids and cabinets on every deck swing on these.

items.name: Patched spare
items.desc: A spare part welded from two broken ones and a prayer. Spine fixers swear by it.
items.notes: The cheap grade: spine buys it, ring does not. Reworks into a standard spare at the bench.

items.name: Pliers
items.desc: Flat jaws, a wire cutter, and polymer grips worn smooth. Bends what the hand cannot. Wears.

items.name: Ceramic tile
items.desc: Fired grey tile, glazed on one side. Floors, benches and furnace walls.

items.name: Crucible liner
items.desc: A fired ceramic cup with a carbon skin. Takes the heat so the smelter does not. Wears.

items.name: Copper bar
items.desc: Dull red bar with a green bloom at the ends. Wire, motors and boards start here.

items.name: Light-metal bar
items.desc: Pale bar with a frosted skin, light for its size. Housings and ring plate start here.

items.name: Pipe
items.desc: A length of steel pipe, threaded at both ends. Water, gas and coolant all run in it.

items.name: Spare part
items.desc: The generic part the station runs on: a cast body, a bush, a gasket. Fits most things badly.
items.notes: What a worn machine (stat_worn) and the foundry system consume. Made at three phases: bench rework (1), fabricator (2), autofab (4).

items.name: Polymer crate
items.desc: A ribbed polymer crate with handholds. Stacks, rinses clean and outlives its contents.

items.name: Bookshelf
items.desc: Plank shelving on an iron frame, bolted to the deck. Books, paper and disc cases.

items.name: Steel cabinet
items.desc: Grey steel, doors that shut, drawers that stick. Holds more than it looks like it should.

items.name: Disc holder
items.desc: Moulded polymer with slots on edge. Floppies and cards, labels facing out.

items.name: Ration bar
items.desc: Grey paste pressed into a bar. Tastes of nothing. Keeps a body going.
items.notes: The staple. The vat presses it from four paste, two bars to a run.

items.name: Sugar
items.desc: White crystals in a twist of foil. Feeds the vat, the still and the galley; children on the spine eat it dry.
items.notes: Feedstock for lux (wine, spirit), med (salves) and life. Sources: vat refining, galley potato pressing.

items.name: Yeast culture
items.desc: A cloudy grey culture in a stoppered tube. Wakes the bread dough and feeds the still.
items.notes: Starter for the vat bakery and dairy discs, and for lux and med fermentation.

items.name: Sliced bread
items.desc: A vat loaf in cling film, sliced eight ways. Grey crumb, pale crust, warm only in the galley.

items.name: Cheese wedge
items.desc: An eighth of a wheel, six slices. Cut it from the thin end with a knife.

items.name: Greens seed
items.desc: A paper twist of pale seed, enough for one tray. Comes up in leaf under the lamp.
items.notes: Hydro harvests return a seed with a chance, so a tray keeps its own stock.

items.name: Bean seed
items.desc: Dry broad beans in a twist of paper. Plant them and more beans come back.

items.name: Seed potato
items.desc: Wrinkled sprouting tubers the size of thumbs. Cut and set, they take root in a tray.

items.name: Herb seed
items.desc: Fine black seed in a screw of foil. Parsley, mostly, or something near it.

items.name: Salad greens
items.desc: Pale leaves grown under a lamp. Limp and bitter, and the nearest thing the spine has to a garden.

items.name: Broad beans
items.desc: Fat pods from the hydro tray, shelled by hand. Plain protein that grows.

items.name: Potatoes
items.desc: Knobbly tubers in a mesh sack, still faintly damp. Cook them or press them for sugar.

items.name: Herb bunch
items.desc: A tied bunch of green herbs. The smell alone is worth a few credits on the spine.

items.name: Paste tube
items.desc: Brown paste in a squeeze tube. Eaten straight from the nozzle on the long shifts.

items.name: Tinned beans
items.desc: Broad beans sealed in a can with a little brine. Nothing on the label but a number.

items.name: Water pouch
items.desc: A litre of clean water in a heat-sealed polymer pouch, cold to the touch.

items.name: Meltwater
items.desc: Ice melted in a bag and strained once. Hard, grey, tastes of iron. Fine for a bunk, better filtered.
items.notes: Ice melted without a filter: cheap spine water, and feed for the purifier.

items.name: Water ration
items.desc: A flat sachet with a day of water in it, stamped with a bunk number. The spine lives on these.

items.name: Water jug
items.desc: Four litres in a sealed polymer jug with a tap. Heavy to carry up a bunk ladder.

items.name: Brine
items.desc: Salt water in a stoppered flask, left over from the cooling loops. Undrinkable, useful to a still.
items.notes: No resident drinks it; it feeds the still, the purifier and the brine algae strain. Source: salvage from the cooling loops.

items.name: Gas canister
items.desc: A steel canister with a screw valve, dented and relabelled. Empty. Fill it, use it, bring it back.
items.notes: Dented canisters turn up in spine salvage; once owned it is a reusable vessel (fill, use, empty).

items.name: Oxygen canister
items.desc: A full canister of breathing gas, green band at the neck. Clinic and Works both stock a rack.

items.name: Foul air bladder
items.desc: A bladder of exhaled air from the bunks, warm and sour. Carbon lives in it. Algae eat it.
items.notes: Collected from bunk vents by scavengers. The scrubber strips its carbon, the algae tank eats it.

items.name: Mask refill
items.desc: A thumb-sized cartridge of breathing gas that clips into a mask. Good for a long shift.

items.name: Air puck
items.desc: A grey puck of salt and carbon that sits in a bunk vent and softens the air. Spent in a month.

items.name: Spent puck
items.desc: A bunk air puck gone dark and heavy with breath. The scrubber can wake it again.
items.notes: Bunk tenants drop these in the ducts. The scrubber regenerates two into two fresh pucks plus a bladder of gas.

items.name: Nutrient mix
items.desc: Grey salts with a little paste stirred in, sold in a twist of film. Hydro feed; the trays drink it.

items.name: Algae mat
items.desc: A wet green mat lifted from the tank, slick and cold. Vat feedstock; it breathes the air clean.

items.name: Water tester
items.desc: A paper strip that turns from yellow to blue in clean water. Brown means do not drink.
items.notes: Used once to check a pouch or a jug. No stat effect yet: a pure information item for the water readout.

items.name: Paper
items.desc: Grey pressed sheet, fibre still visible in the grain. Takes print, folds, burns.

items.name: Spun yarn
items.desc: A hank of fibre twisted tight on the bench. Weave it, knit it or braid it into a wick.

items.name: Wick
items.desc: A braided thread of yarn, stiff with use. A candle or a lamp is no good without one.

items.name: Wine must
items.desc: Sweet cloudy mash in a flask, working slowly. It is wine if you leave it alone.

items.name: Sugar wash
items.desc: Sugar and grey water gone sour in a flask. Sharp, thin, and only good for the still.

items.name: Wine bottle
items.desc: Dark green glass, no year on it. Hold it to the light to see how much is left.
items.notes: Pinned composition includes its glass; the still recipe consumes a bottle plus must. Empty vessel returns via the recycler.

items.name: Spirit bottle
items.desc: Clear and fierce, run twice through the still. Sold sealed, with a company stamp on the cap.

items.name: Moonshine
items.desc: Algae mash run through a still nobody admits to. Cloudy, burns going down, cheap.
items.notes: Spine product: brewed without a vintner licence. Also sold by sellers who run their own still.

items.name: Book
items.desc: Leather-bound, the title worn off. Paper is getting rare.
items.notes: The old kind: nobody makes these. Printed books are the craft version.

items.name: Dice
items.desc: Two cubes of polymer, the dots drilled by hand. One of them runs a little heavy.

items.name: Locket
items.desc: Gold, and the hinge still closes. What is inside was someone else's.
items.notes: Carried item. The jeweller card can set new ones, but the old ones are worth keeping.

items.name: Candle
items.desc: A taper of wax and a wick: light when the power is out.
items.notes: Fire is banned aboard. Residents still buy them quietly; the fence trades them.

items.name: Matchbox
items.desc: Ten matches when new. The drawer shows how many are left.

items.name: Match
items.desc: One strike's worth of light.

items.name: Disposable lighter
items.desc: Cheap plastic, every one a different colour. When it runs out, it is rubbish.

items.name: Refillable lighter
items.desc: Brushed chrome, a lid that clicks. Fill it with lamp oil or spirit.
items.notes: Holds one flask of fluid; spirit also works.

items.name: Lighter fluid
items.desc: A flask of thin, sweet-smelling solvent. Refills a zippo or feeds a lamp. Do not keep it near a vent.

items.name: Flint striker
items.desc: A bar of iron and rare earth with a steel scraper. Throws sparks into tinder on the first stroke.
items.notes: Spine alternative to matches: lasts years.

items.name: Oil lamp
items.desc: A glass chimney on a light-metal body with a braided wick. Burns oil, smells of it, and it gives a real flame.
items.notes: Takes lamp oil or fluid (food oil also burns).

items.name: Old photograph
items.desc: A printed face in a paper frame, silvered with age. Nobody alive can say who it is.
items.notes: No recipe. Salvage and sellers only.

items.name: Wristwatch
items.desc: Wound movement in a steel case. It runs eleven minutes slow and nobody would change that.
items.notes: No recipe: only sellers (collectors) bring them.

items.name: Lubricant
items.desc: A squeeze tube of clear grease, smelling of oil and warm plastic. A little keeps a feed from jamming.
items.notes: Ten tubes per batch; the cheap route runs carbon through the chem bench (rcp_mach_brew_lubricant_cheap) and is not written, see notes in recipes.

items.name: Water filter
items.desc: A grey carbon-and-mesh cartridge in a polymer sleeve. The purifier runs through it; it clogs slowly.
items.notes: Spine bunks fit one over the tap to make tap water drinkable, which is why they buy it as parts.

items.name: Air cartridge
items.desc: A flat carbon-packed cartridge with a fibre pre-screen. Slots into a scrubber; bunks clip them over the vent.
items.notes: Serves need_air directly: one cartridge is one resident-day of cleaner air for a bunk.

items.name: Spent water filter
items.desc: A clogged cartridge, heavy and brown with trapped grime. Rinse it with clean water, or recycle it.
items.notes: The sludge is what the filter caught. rcp_mach_rinse_water_filter turns it back into a filter, a greywater and the sludge. Also turns up in salvage lots, so a rinse loop can start before the first filter wears out.

items.name: Spent air cartridge
items.desc: The carbon bed is black and full. It rattles when shaken. Rinse it, or send it to the recycler.
items.notes: rcp_mach_rinse_air_cartridge restores it. Also turns up in salvage lots, so a rinse loop can start before the first filter wears out.

items.name: Jam kit
items.desc: A roll of picks, a bent probe and a squeeze of grease. Frees a clogged feed without a wrench.
items.notes: A tool in rcp_mach_clear_jam_kit; wears out after four jobs.

items.name: Fuse
items.desc: A glass tube with a thin copper filament, packed in grit. It dies first so the machine does not.
items.notes: Clears a tripped breaker.

items.name: Sealing tape
items.desc: A reel of grey polymer tape with a hard adhesive. A box sealed with it opens only under a knife.
items.notes: The sealer eats one per small or medium box, two per large.

items.name: Padding
items.desc: Shredded rag packed in a flat bag. Stuffed round the goods it keeps a box from arriving dented.
items.notes: Made by hand from rags. Also hides things: see rcp_mach_hide_in_box.

items.name: Label roll
items.desc: A roll of gummed paper strips, blank, with a hole for the labeller spindle.
items.notes: Cut on the slip printer from a sheet of paper. One roll per label.

items.name: Cleaning kit
items.desc: A rag, a brush and a vial of solvent in a pouch. Lifts dust and gum from the works of a machine.
items.notes: Households use it too, hence need_comfort.

items.name: Painkiller
items.desc: White tablet, scored once. Takes the edge off a sore back and a long shift.

items.name: Antibiotic
items.desc: Yellow capsule-shaped tablet. Course of six; the clinic counts them back.

items.name: Sleeping pill
items.desc: Small blue tablet. Eight dull hours and a clear head, if the pipes allow.

items.name: Blister card
items.desc: Empty foil card of six pockets. Pills push out through the back and do not go back in.
items.notes: Empty card. Filled cards are separate items (it_med_fb_*) with container.fill of six pills.

items.name: Bandage
items.desc: Gauze roll with a steel clip. Boiled and re-rolled until it frays.

items.name: Antiseptic
items.desc: Brown dropper bottle of ethanol and iodine salts. Stings, which is the point.

items.name: Stim
items.desc: Orange tablet, bitter. A shift of borrowed energy, repaid with interest the next morning.
items.notes: Pressed at 5 per reagent unit: the margin is above 6x on purpose, a stim is the dear end of the bench.

items.name: Burn tab
items.desc: Grey tablet of carbon and reagent. Eases scald and weld flash pain for a few hours.

items.name: Energy tab
items.desc: Sugar and a pinch of reagent pressed into a sweet tablet. A small lift, no hangover.
items.notes: The mild stim: +1 now and no status, so no crash. Cheap enough to be the spine's habit.

items.name: Gauze pad
items.desc: Square of loose-woven gauze, folded twice. Sterile until the packet is opened.

items.name: Rehydration mix
items.desc: Sachet of sugar and salt to stir into a pouch of water. Ends the shakes after a bad vent shift.

items.name: Dream tab
items.desc: Unmarked white tablet with a soft sweet taste. A warm, loose day in a body that is owed none.
items.notes: Contraband (drug). Sold through res_fence and the black market; the premium is in the market, not in value.

items.name: Blue ampoule
items.desc: Sealed glass ampoule of blue solution. Snap, swallow, and the station goes quiet for an hour.
items.notes: Contraband (drug). The strong one: +2 energy now, the same crash tomorrow.

items.name: Dream blister
items.desc: Six unmarked tablets in plain foil. No stamp, no maker, no questions.
items.notes: Composition includes the card and its six pills; container.fill lists them for taking out.

items.name: Small cell
items.desc: A thumb-thick cell in a grey sleeve, stamped 10. Runs a hot plate or a printer for a morning.
items.notes: Phase 1 fuel: also brought by walk-in sellers (task 10 lists it in sells). Replaces coal; a spent cell is not a separate item, charge is state.

items.name: Cell
items.desc: Ribbed steel case, a charge gauge scratched into the side. Fuels the mid-size machines for a day.
items.notes: Crate stock until the cell press (phase 3) can make it.

items.name: Heavy cell
items.desc: A forearm of sealed lithium in a light-metal jacket. It runs a press or a mainframe, and weighs like one.

items.name: Circuit board
items.desc: Green board, hand-soldered, flux still tacky. Every device on the station starts from one.

items.name: Grow lamp
items.desc: Hydro light: a glass tube on a copper base. A tool, and it dims a little every night it burns.
items.notes: Hydro trays need one from day 1, so it arrives by crate before the fabricator exists.

items.name: Motor
items.desc: Small electric motor: a copper winding round an iron rotor, and a hum. Fans, belts and loaders turn on it.

items.name: Sensor
items.desc: Reads gas, heat or light through a pinhole of glass. Scanners and scrubbers listen to it.

items.name: Cable
items.desc: Sheathed cable, a metre of copper inside grey polymer. Joins everything to everything else.

items.name: Order slip
items.desc: A strip of thermal paper: sender, goods, pay on delivery. A box leaves the dock only with one inside.
items.notes: Its sink is the box rule (SEED 6.6), not a recipe; the recycler is its only other use, so a recycle-only warning is expected.

items.name: Switch
items.desc: A thumb switch: brass blade, polymer rocker, two screws. It clicks like a lock.

items.name: Torch
items.desc: A polymer tube, a switch and a lamp. The legal light: no flame, no smoke, no inspector at the door.
items.notes: The lawful answer to candles and matches (contraband fire). Takes a small cell in the field.

items.name: Notice poster
items.desc: Hard print, one colour: RATIONS AT SIX, KEEP THE DUCT CLEAR. Pinned up in every spine corridor.

discs.name: Hydro greens
discs.desc: Grow charts for leaves, beans, potatoes, herbs and tomatoes on a tray or a rack.
discs.label: HYDRO / GREENS BEANS ROOTS

discs.name: Blank floppy
discs.desc: A 3.5-inch floppy with a white label and nothing on it. Whatever you copy to it needs a terminal to read.
discs.label: BLANK
discs.notes: Carried over from the old blank floppy. Copy target for any copyable floppy.

discs.name: Salvaged disc
discs.desc: An unlabelled disc with a sticking shutter. Diaries, logs and schedules from somebody else's life.

data_effects.text: Read it: rumours are 5% more often right
Collectors pay 10% over for dead people's files

discs.label: (NO LABEL)
discs.notes: src/discs/unlabelled.md. Sells to collectors as a curiosity; also the mild source of rumours.

discs.name: Mail client
discs.desc: The company's mail disc: orders, attachments and the daily memo. No modem, no mail.
discs.label:
COMPANY MAIL 1.0
MAIL.EXE

discs.name: Labels disc
discs.desc: Prints order slips and shelf labels on the slip printer. Dot-matrix font, three sizes.
discs.label:
LABELS 1.2
LABELS.EXE

discs.name: Pixel paint
discs.desc: An orange shareware disc with a brush and a little sun on a hand-drawn label. Copy me, it says.
discs.label:
PIXEL PAINT 2.1
SHAREWARE: COPY ME
discs.notes: src/discs/paint.md. Exempt from the upgrade route (novelty).

discs.name: Mines
discs.desc: A grey disc, ten kilobytes of dread. Flag the mines. Do not step on the mines.
discs.label: MINES 1.0
discs.notes: src/discs/mines.md. Exempt from the upgrade route (novelty).

discs.name: Stocktake Pro
discs.desc: A green disc in a hard case with a hologram sticker. The case says LICENSED SOFTWARE.
discs.label:
STOCKTAKE PRO 4
LICENSED SOFTWARE
SERIAL 0441-7782-K
discs.notes: src/discs/stock.md. It starts only with this disc in drive A:, so the licence is the disc.

discs.name: Tracker and chess
discs.desc: A scuffed disc of module tunes and a chess board. Somebody scratched a clef into the plastic.
discs.label:
TRACKER 1.0 + CHESS
SHAREWARE
discs.notes: Sold by an upgrade; also turns up through salvage and seller.

upgrades.name: Workbench crate
upgrades.desc: Crated on the outside counter. Repair, refill, bundle, refurbish. ECONOMY.md's workbench.

upgrades.name: Smelter crate
upgrades.desc: Crated on the outside counter. The old furnace on cells: two ore into one bar, slag out.

upgrades.name: Recycler crate
upgrades.desc: Any item into its materials as unit items; 10% to sludge. Generic rule, no written recipes.

upgrades.name: Crusher crate
upgrades.desc: Breaks mixed scrap, e-waste and ice into sorted unit items, better than the recycler for raw lots.

upgrades.name: Purifier crate
upgrades.desc: Crated on the outside counter. Greywater or ice into clean water; a filter wears.

upgrades.name: Charger crate
upgrades.desc: Crated on the outside counter. Refills spent cells from station power; billed in credits at the power price.

upgrades.name: Hydro tray crate
upgrades.desc: Crated on the outside counter. Seed, water, nutrient and a lamp; grows over nights.

upgrades.name: Wired terminal crate
upgrades.desc: Crated on the outside counter. Runs programs from discs; mail, orders, remote for machines.

upgrades.name: Modem crate
upgrades.desc: Crated on the outside counter. Plugs into the terminal: mail, orders, boards. No modem, no mail.

upgrades.name: Slip printer crate
upgrades.desc: Crated on the outside counter. Small print surface: order slips, labels, receipts.

upgrades.name: Box sealer crate
upgrades.desc: Crated on the outside counter. Seals a packed box (mod_sealed). A sealed box opens only with a knife.

upgrades.name: Scanner crate
upgrades.desc: Reveals hidden modifiers (virus, counterfeit), composition and contraband flags.

upgrades.name: Radio crate
upgrades.desc: Crated on the outside counter. Engineers' chatter: rumors earlier and likelier right. Effects only.

upgrades.name: Hydro greens disc
upgrades.desc: Floppy by mail. Greens, sprouts, beans.

upgrades.name: Mail program disc
upgrades.desc: Floppy by mail. Mail and orders.

upgrades.name: Labels program disc
upgrades.desc: Floppy by mail. Prints order slips and labels.

upgrades.name: Tracker and chess disc
upgrades.desc: Floppy by mail. Module tunes and a chess board.

upgrades.name: Shop extension
upgrades.desc: Knock through the next bay along: four more columns of floor, then four more rows.

upgrades.name: Dock extension
upgrades.desc: Two more rows on the dock grid and, later, two more columns: more boxes per pickup.

upgrades.name: Folding cot
upgrades.desc: Canvas on a steel frame, set up behind the stock. One decent night changes the morning.

upgrades.name: Display case
upgrades.desc: Glass-fronted, lit from inside. Things behind glass are worth what the buyer imagines.

upgrades.name: Shelf unit
upgrades.desc: Open steel shelving, bolted to the deck. Holds whatever you stack on it.

upgrades.name: Bookshelf
upgrades.desc: Another bookshelf, for paper and anything flat. Opening it takes a window.

upgrades.name: Steel cabinet
upgrades.desc: A grey cabinet that holds more than it looks. Doors shut; things stay put.

upgrades.name: Disc holder
upgrades.desc: A polymer rack with slots for floppies and cards. Keeps the labels facing out.

upgrades.name: Ledger book
upgrades.desc: A bound book and a pencil on a string. Each evening you write down what sold and why.

upgrades.name: Pigeonholes
upgrades.desc: A wall of paper slots for slips and notices. Senders find a shop that answers.

upgrades.name: Shop sign
upgrades.desc: Stencilled letters on a lit panel above the shutter. The corridor starts to know your name.

upgrades.name: Memory bank
upgrades.desc: Four chips on a card, pressed into the terminal's spare socket. More windows, fewer refusals.

residents.name: Bunk tenant
residents.desc: Fourth bunk up on the spine. Counts water by the cup and air by the shift.
lines: Water first. The rest I can do without.
Is that a spine price or a ring price?
Row C is out of pucks again. Anything cheaper?
Pay you Friday. No? Then half now.

residents.name: Duct scavenger
residents.desc: Crawls the spine ducts with a sack. Sells what the company wrote off.
lines: Found it behind a panel. Don't ask which panel.
Three credits, or a filter. Your pick.
Heirloom. Somebody's gran, probably. Probably dead.

residents.name: Dock hauler
residents.desc: Rides the ore and ice tugs. Brings raw goods in, takes cells and parts out.
lines: Ore on the dock by nine. Cells by ten, or I walk.
Tug came in short. Prices follow.
I sell what the rock gives. You sell what the rock costs.

residents.name: Foundry fitter
residents.desc: Keeps the rolling mills turning. Hard on tools, harder on hands.
lines: Wrench gave out mid-pour. Got another?
Burn gel, two. Foreman's counting.
Works pays Fridays. Credit's good till then.

residents.name: Smelter hand
residents.desc: Walks out of the foundry with bars, slag and a thirst. Trades both.
lines: Bars off the second pour. Don't ask whose.
Got a still behind the cooling rack. Interested?
Something for the burns. And something for the head.

residents.name: Station technician
residents.desc: Fixes whatever the mid decks break. Collects circuits and discs.
lines: Got a floppy? Mine went bad on the third copy.
Circuits. Anything that isn't scorched.
If it has a screen it comes to me first.

residents.name: Clinic orderly
residents.desc: Buys stock for the clinic out of a ledger that never balances.
lines: Pharmacy is one order behind. Always.
Not for me. For ward two.
Antiseptic or nothing. We boil the rest.

residents.name: Reactor engineer
residents.desc: Sleeps beside the plant. Trades cells and chips, and talks too much.
lines: Pump three is chattering. Told them last week.
Take the cells. And don't quote me on the load.
If the lights flicker twice, buy early.

residents.name: Company clerk
residents.desc: Stamps what the company allows. Buys paper, comfort and licensed software.
lines: Is that licensed? I have to ask.
Slips. Forty. The forms never end.
I did not see that. Officially I saw it.

residents.name: Ring household
residents.desc: A ring family with real soil and a view. Pays well and wants it now.
lines: Is it real? We can tell.
Name your price. Then deliver by Thursday.
The glass needs a pane. Today, if you can.

residents.name: Fence
residents.desc: Moves what should not move: fire, drugs, cracked software, stolen stock.
lines: Never seen you. Never saw this either.
Fire's worth three times what it burns.
Ask me no questions, pay me no tax.

orders.name: Water for the row
orders.text: Four jugs and two bars. Pay on delivery, not before.

orders.name: Last puck on row C
orders.text: Row C is down to its last puck. Whatever you can spare.

orders.name: Weekly rations
orders.text: Same as last week. Same as every week.

orders.name: Scrubber bank is down
orders.text: Bank 4 has stopped. Filters, any filters, today.
orders.notes: Spawned by the scrubber failure events; weight 0 in the normal draw.

orders.name: Tools for the ducts
orders.text: A knife, pliers, tape. Duct work eats all three.

orders.name: Cells and cable
orders.text: Three small cells and cable. I will trade scrap if you prefer.

orders.name: Tug stores
orders.text: Stores for the next run. Eight bars, four tins, four jugs.

orders.name: Tools for the second shift
orders.text: Two wrenches, a jam kit, grease. Foreman signs on delivery.

orders.name: Spent water filters
orders.text: Four spent filters. The shop rewinds them for the cooling loop.

orders.name: Shift meds
orders.text: Pills for the hands and something for the burns.

orders.name: Yeast and sugar
orders.text: Yeast, sugar. For the bread. Honestly.
orders.notes: Also what a still wants; the buyer says bread.

orders.name: Circuit stock
orders.text: Anything that works. Test them first.

orders.name: Blank floppies
orders.text: Blank floppies, three. Not the ones with the bad sector.

orders.name: Algae tanks
orders.text: Tank two is browning. Nutrient, starter, a fresh sensor.

orders.name: Ward stock
orders.text: Standard ward restock. Count them twice.

orders.name: Cells for the crew
orders.text: Cells, charged. Core crew burns them in a night.

orders.name: Form slips
orders.text: Twenty slips and two label rolls. The forms never end.

orders.name: Paper and ledgers
orders.text: Paper, ledgers, a notice board sheet. Company stock.

orders.name: Lighters
orders.text: Lighters, fluid, a striker. Fire sells.

orders.name: Company tithe, phase 1
orders.text: Tithe for the week: forty credits of rations to the company store. Late tithe is docked from wages.
orders.notes: One tithe template per phase; the want is a need value, book rate 0.25 of market. Penalty is soft by default (STATION 7).

orders.name: Rent due
orders.text: Rent is due on the stall. Five a day. Late rent is added to the tithe.
orders.notes: Memo, no wants. Phase 1 rent is 5 a day.

orders.name: Wage notice
orders.text: Wage scale adjustments take effect next cycle. Complaints to the clerk.

orders.name: Clinic staples
orders.text: Quarterly staples. Please send in one box.

orders.name: Weekly dressings
orders.text: Weekly dressings, same as before.

orders.name: Strike notice
orders.text: Works hands down tools at the next shift. Parts will be slow.

orders.name: Filter returns
orders.text: Spent filters and pucks, back for the recycler. Weights agreed.

orders.name: A complaint
orders.text: The council notes with regret that deliveries to the ring are late.

orders.name: Pickup notice
orders.text: Next general pickup is posted. Sealed boxes in the dock by then.

orders.name: Packing stock
orders.text: Crates, padding, tape. We run short every week.

orders.name: FREE WINE inside
orders.text: Free wine, free music, free everything. Open the disc.
orders.notes: Spam: the attached disc carries mod_infected.

orders.name: Inspection notice
orders.text: An inspection of stalls on the mid decks is scheduled. Declare nothing, hide nothing.

events.name: Reactor scram

rumor.text: Core engineer: the coolant pump is chattering. We may scram.

events.mail_text: Reactor scrammed. Cells are rationed until the plant restarts.

events.name: Dust on the vanes

rumor.text: Board: a dust cloud is crossing the vanes. Expect dimmer light.

events.mail_text: Dust storm across the sails. Ring power is thin.

events.name: Scrubber bank fails

rumor.text: Engineer: bank 4 is on its last cartridges. It will not last the week.

events.mail_text: Scrubber bank 4 has failed. Air is thin on the spine.

events.name: Cartridge shortage

rumor.text: Board: queue at the filter stand. Cartridges rumoured out.

events.mail_text: Replacement cartridges are gone. Filters sell at any price.

events.name: Algae die-off

rumor.text: Board: tank temperatures are climbing on the mid decks.

events.mail_text: The mid-deck algae tanks have browned. Air and food are short.

events.name: Sludge in the tanks

rumor.text: Engineer: the reclaim loop is sluggish. The sludge count is up.

events.mail_text: Reclaim tanks are fouled with sludge. Water is rationed.

events.name: Ice tug lost

rumor.text: Radio: an ice tug is overdue and out of contact.

events.mail_text: The ice tug did not return. Water will be dear.

events.name: Vat contamination

rumor.text: Board: union reports a smell in vat room three.

events.mail_text: The vats are contaminated. Rations are short and the clinic fills.

events.name: Foundry strike

rumor.text: Board: union voted to stop work at the next shift.

events.mail_text: The works has downed tools. Parts will be slow.

events.name: Foundry backlog
events.mail_text: The foundry is clearing its backlog. Bars flood the dock.

events.name: Ore convoy late

rumor.text: Radio: the ore convoy is overdue. Cause unknown.

events.mail_text: The ore convoy is late. The foundry is idle.

events.name: Clinic stock-out

rumor.text: Orderly: the pharmacy is one order behind. It will be more.

events.mail_text: The clinic has run out of antibiotics. Private sellers are busy.

events.name: Store restock cut

rumor.text: Clerk: stock sheets are coming in thinner. Make of that what you will.

events.mail_text: The company store is cutting its range. Lamps and cushions sell out.

events.name: Ore convoy lands

rumor.text: Radio: ore convoy inbound, heavy load.

events.mail_text: An ore convoy has docked. Raw metal is cheap this week.

events.name: Ice convoy lands

rumor.text: Radio: tugs bring a full load of ice. Water will ease.

events.mail_text: Comet ice is in. Water is plentiful for a while.

events.name: Ration convoy

rumor.text: Board: halls overran the quota. Rations to go out cheap.

events.mail_text: Vat halls ship a surplus of rations. Prices fall.

events.name: Fever

rumor.text: Orderly: beds are filling with the same symptoms.

events.mail_text: A fever has reached the lower decks. Medicine is in demand.

events.name: Gut sickness
events.mail_text: Bad vat food has sent half the works to bed.

events.name: Works feast

rumor.text: Board: union feast tonight in the hall. Bring a dish.

events.mail_text: The union has called a feast. Food and a little drink are wanted.

events.name: Routine inspection

rumor.text: Security: an inspection of mid-deck stalls has been scheduled.

events.mail_text: Security is inspecting stalls on the mid decks. Anything flagged is seized.

events.name: Works wage cut

rumor.text: Union: the company may cut scales next cycle.

events.mail_text: The company cuts works wages. Fewer coins for everything.

events.name: Spine ration cut

rumor.text: Board: allowance schedule for the spine is under revision.

events.mail_text: The company reduces spine credit allowance. Bunks tighten belts.

events.name: Corridor breach
events.mail_text: A corridor was breached overnight. Everyone is tired.

events.name: Salvage drift

rumor.text: Radio: a wreck is drifting close to the dock.

events.mail_text: A salvage drift is in range. Scrap floods the ducts.

events.name: Stim shipment
events.mail_text: A stim shipment arrives. A short sharp day, then a crash.

events.name: Company feast

rumor.text: Board: store hosts a meal for staff and tenants.

events.mail_text: The company hosts a feast. Even the stalls get a meal.

events.name: Quiet cycle
events.mail_text: A quiet cycle. No alarms, no queues, a clear head.
